text: Creation order: archetype, drives, drive statements, skills, focus, talent, gear, name, appearance, personal agenda.
Assign the values 8, 7, 6, 5 and 4 to the five drives (DUTY, FAITH, JUSTICE, POWER, TRUTH), one value each: 30 points in all.
The lowest drive is 4.
The highest drive is 8.
Your archetype’s key drive is a suggestion for where the 8 goes; it follows the same cap.
Write a one-line statement for every drive rated 6 or more (pre-generated agents carry one for all five). A test may only use a drive whose statement fits the action.
Distribute 26 points among the five skills: BATTLE, COMMUNICATE, DISCIPLINE, MOVE, UNDERSTAND.
No skill may start below 4.
Key skills may start at up to 8.
Other skills may also start at up to 8; most characters keep them at 4–6.
Pick two focuses (a narrow specialty such as "Poisons" or "Short blades"). A focused test scores two successes on any die up to the skill rating.
Pick one talent from your archetype, or one general talent.
Take the archetype’s fixed items and one item from each choice line. Add one personal item of Quality 0–1.
A character can take 8 Stress. At 8 they are taken out and roll on the consequence table.
Remove all Stress after a scene of rest; a Suk doctor or Field Surgery removes 2 at once.
Target number = drive + skill.
Roll 2d20. Buy up to three more d20 with Momentum (1, 2, then 3) or by giving the Narrator Threat. Maximum 5d20.
Difficulty 0 Simple, 1 Average, 2 Challenging, 3 Daunting, 4 Dire, 5 Epic.
A natural 1 is two successes. With an applicable focus, any die up to the skill rating is two successes.
A natural 20 is a complication. Hostile conditions widen the range down to 16–20.
The players share a Momentum pool capped at 6. Unspent Momentum drops by 1 at the end of each scene.
Spend Momentum to buy d20s (1/2/3), Obtain Information (1), Create a Trait (2), inflict extra Stress (1 each), or Keep the Initiative (2).
The Narrator starts each session with 2 Threat per player.
Threat grows when players buy dice with it, when a complication is converted (2 Threat), and when the characters act openly against a powerful faction.

The Narrator spends Threat on NPC dice (1/2/3), +1 Difficulty (2), complications or environment effects (2), changing a trait (2), reinforcements (each creature lists its cost), and rival House actions (1).
In a conflict the acting side passes the turn to the other side, or pays 2 Momentum (players) / 2 Threat (Narrator) to act again at +1 Difficulty.
Assets (weapons, gear, contacts, secrets) have Quality 0–4. An asset of Quality 3+ grants one free bonus d20 when it is decisive (weapons: stats.bonus).
Shields stop fast attacks. A blade attacker spends 1 Momentum for a slow strike to pass a shield. A lasgun hitting a shield causes a pseudo-atomic blast.
Conflicts are duels, skirmishes, warfare, espionage or intrigue. Each is divided into zones; in intrigue every zone is adjacent.

value.name: Duel
value.text: Two combatants in one zone; shields make the slow strike the only way through.

value.name: Skirmish
value.text: Small groups across several zones; movement, cover and assets matter.

value.name: Warfare
value.text: Armies are assets; characters lead, scout or strike key targets.

value.name: Espionage
value.text: Infiltration and counter-intelligence; exposure is tracked as a clock.

value.name: Intrigue
value.text: Words as weapons; all zones are adjacent; secrets and leverage are assets.

text: When taken out, roll 1d20 on the consequence table (injuries.json). Consequences replace hit-point injuries: wounds, poison, dehydration, exposure and disgrace.
Dune does not track encumbrance by weight. Weight is shown for flavor; the Narrator vetoes absurd loads.
